V0001.line: GS2 | Polity | Salient features of the Representation of People's Act
V0001.title: Representation of the People Act 1950, UPSC Notes
facts: RPA 1950 covers seat allocation for Lok Sabha, State Assemblies and Councils, delimitation, voter qualifications, electoral rolls and the manner of filling seats.
Its four Schedules: First, Lok Sabha seats and SC/ST reservation; Second, Assembly strength per State; Third, Council seats; Fourth, local authorities electing to Councils.
Articles 82 and 170 require Lok Sabha and Assembly seats to be readjusted after each census.
A voter must be 18 on the qualifying date and ordinarily resident in the constituency; nobody may be enrolled in two constituencies or twice in one.
Barred from registration: non-citizens, persons declared of unsound mind by a competent court, and persons disqualified under corrupt-practice or election-offence laws.
Each State's Chief Electoral Officer, designated by the ECI in consultation with the State, supervises preparation, revision and correction of all rolls.
The District Election Officer coordinates roll work in a district; the Electoral Registration Officer prepares and revises each constituency's roll.
A Parliamentary constituency's roll is made up of the rolls of all its Assembly constituencies, prepared under ECI superintendence.
Election Laws (Amendment) Act 2021: Aadhaar may be sought to establish identity, four qualifying dates a year (1 Jan, 1 Apr, 1 Jul, 1 Oct), 'spouse' replaces 'wife'.
Civil courts cannot decide a person's entitlement to be enrolled or question an ERO's action; roll offences by officers need an ECI or CEO complaint.
The Law Commission supports the ECI proposal of a common electoral roll for Parliament, Assembly and local body elections.

V0002.line: GS2 | Polity | Salient features of the Representation of People's Act
V0002.title: Special Intensive Revision (SIR), Meaning, Phases, Latest News 2026
facts: SIR is the ECI's time-bound house-to-house re-verification of rolls, unlike routine summary revision; Booth Level Officers hand out and collect enumeration forms.
SIR steps: notification with a qualifying date, house visits, data checks, draft roll, claims and objections, notice and hearing, then final roll.
Form 6 is for inclusion, Form 7 for objection or deletion, Form 8 for correction or shifting residence.
Article 324 vests superintendence of roll preparation in the ECI; Article 326 provides adult suffrage subject to legal disqualifications.
RPA 1950: Section 16 bars non-citizens; Section 19 ties enrolment to age and ordinary residence; Section 21(3) allows a special revision anytime for recorded reasons.
Section 22 lets EROs correct, transpose or delete entries after verification; the procedure is in the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.
Phase I in Bihar (June-September 2025) cut the electorate from 7.89 crore to about 7.42 crore.
Phase II covered 9 States and 3 UTs (about 51 crore electors); Phase III covers 16 States and 3 UTs with over 3.94 lakh BLOs.
On 27 May 2026 the Supreme Court (ADR vs ECI) held SIR within the ECI's statutory mandate and consistent with free and fair elections.
BLOs make two to three visits before an elector is treated as untraceable; appeals go to the designated appellate authority and then the CEO.

V0003.line: GS2 | Polity | Salient features of the Representation of People's Act
V0003.title: SC Upholds Special Intensive Revision (SIR)
facts: The Supreme Court upheld the Bihar SIR and allowed similar exercises in other States and UTs.
The Court described Article 324 as a continuing source of ECI power to protect the electoral process at every stage.
It accepted the ECI's grounds: urbanisation, migration, unreported deaths and duplicate entries after more than two decades without an intensive revision.
Enrolment in a roll is only a rebuttable presumption of citizenship, not conclusive proof.
Safeguards ordered: published lists of excluded names with reasons, notice and hearing, and judicial remedies against wrongful deletion.
Persons deleted for absence, duplication, death, shifting or citizenship doubts may challenge the ECI decision before competent courts.
Critics fear disenfranchisement and a blurring of electoral administration with citizenship determination; supporters cite cleaner rolls and wider Article 324 scope.
The Bench held that electoral rolls are not static and must change with demographic and residential shifts.

V0004.line: GS2 | Polity | Salient features of the Representation of People's Act
V0004.title: Special Summary Revision: Key Differences Between SSR and SIR
facts: Special Summary Revision is the ECI's routine roll update: it adds newly eligible voters and removes dead or shifted electors.
Under SSR existing voters stay enrolled unless due process supports deletion; SIR asks electors to re-establish eligibility.
Section 21(2) of RPA 1950 requires roll revision before every general election and in any year the ECI directs, with reference to a qualifying date.
Rolls are prepared constituency-wise with the Electoral Registration Officer as the statutory authority, under Article 324, RPA 1950 and the 1960 Rules.

V0005.line: GS2 | Polity | Salient features of the Representation of People's Act
V0005.title: Ordinarily Resident, Meaning, Rules, Definition
facts: Section 19 of RPA 1950 allows enrolment only of a person ordinarily resident in the constituency.
Section 20 defines ordinarily resident: merely owning or possessing a house in a constituency does not make a person ordinarily resident there.
Spouses of persons with a service qualification are also treated as ordinarily resident in the original constituency.
Section 20A, added in 2010, lets Non-Resident Indians register at the address in their passport while living abroad.
